classification.difficultyReason: Divide the production total by each bag size and identify quotient as complete bags and remainder as leftovers; both outputs are explicitly requested.

content.prompt: A humbug-making machine produced $12\,429$ humbugs in three days.

children.label: a
children.prompt: How many bags of 8 is this? How many are left over?

answer.worked:
$$\begin{array}{r|rrrrr}& &1&5&5&3\\\hline 8&1&2&{}^{4}4&{}^{4}2&{}^{2}9\end{array}$$

$12\,429\div8=1553\text{ remainder }5$.

Check: $8\times1553+5=12\,429$.

1553 bags can be filled, with 5 humbugs left over.

children.label: b
children.prompt: How many mega-bags of 36 is this? How many are left over?

answer.worked:
$$\begin{array}{r|r}&345\\\hline36&\begin{array}{rrrrr}1&2&4&2&9\\1&0&8&&\\\hline&1&6&2&\\&1&4&4&\\\hline&&1&8&9\\&&1&8&0\\\hline&&&&9\end{array}\end{array}$$

$12\,429\div36=345\text{ remainder }9$.

Check: $36\times345+9=12\,429$.

345 mega-bags can be filled, with 9 humbugs left over.
